reason: All 12 criteria met. The one gap from iteration 1 — /audit-build's citation heading still reading as an imperative — was fixed by the Debug stage and re-verified here.

criteria.statement: When an audit deletes something because nothing in the source asks for it, the readout labels it DELETED, never the imperative DELETE
criteria.cites: Intended Change table row: DELETE -> DELETED ('the audit removes it')
criteria.reason: The heading reads 'DELETED — nothing in the source asked for these' in all four /audit-trd and /audit-prd layers; the imperative form has zero occurrences across the six audit files and their .claude runtime mirrors.

criteria.statement: When the audit lowers a value to the constitution floor because no reason was given for exceeding it, the readout reads 'LOWERED TO THE CONSTITUTION FLOOR — no reason was given for exceeding it'; when a reason WAS given, no finding of this kind is raised
criteria.cites: Intended Change table row: 'LOWER TO THE CONSTITUTION FLOOR, or say why it's higher' -> past-tense one-way form
criteria.reason: The past-tense heading appears verbatim in all four layers; the two-way imperative form ('LOWER TO THE CONSTITUTION FLOOR') has zero occurrences.

criteria.statement: When the audit restores something in the source but missing from the document, the readout labels it ADDED BACK, never the imperative ADD BACK
criteria.cites: Intended Change table row: ADD BACK -> ADDED BACK
criteria.reason: 'ADDED BACK — in the source, missing from this <doc>' present in all four layers; 'ADD BACK —' has zero occurrences.

criteria.statement: When the audit fixes a citation whose referenced ID does not resolve, the readout labels it FIXED THE CITATION, never the imperative FIX THE CITATION
criteria.cites: Intended Change table row: FIX THE CITATION -> FIXED THE CITATION ('mechanical')
criteria.reason: This was the single gap from iteration 1: /audit-build still carried the imperative. The Debug stage renamed it and also narrowed the claim (the fix applies only inside this run's own rewrite of the Could Not Verify section; a citation that does not resolve elsewhere is reported, not fixed). Independent grep for the literal 'FIX THE CITATION' across all six files and their .claude mirrors now returns zero.

criteria.statement: When the audit corrects a stale claim in favour of what the code does, the readout labels it CORRECTED A STALE CLAIM, never the assertion THE DOC IS STALE
criteria.cites: Intended Change table row: THE DOC IS STALE -> CORRECTED A STALE CLAIM
criteria.reason: 'CORRECTED A STALE CLAIM' present in all four layers; 'THE DOC IS STALE' has zero occurrences.

criteria.statement: A task judged unbuildable-as-written renders as one of two distinct headings — 'REDESIGNED — could not be built as written' or 'CANNOT BE BUILT — needs a design decision' — never the single undifferentiated CANNOT BE BUILT AS WRITTEN
criteria.cites: Intended Change table row: CANNOT BE BUILT AS WRITTEN 'splits in two'
criteria.reason: Both headings are defined in /audit-trd's workflow script and command prompt (adjacent lines in each); the old single heading has zero occurrences anywhere.

criteria.statement: A contradiction still renders as the imperative 'PICK ONE — these contradict', unchanged
criteria.cites: Intended Change table row: 'PICK ONE — these contradict' -> unchanged
criteria.reason: Present verbatim and unmodified in all four layers.

criteria.statement: A finding asking whether something is actually wanted still renders as the imperative CONFIRM THESE ARE WANTED, unchanged
criteria.cites: Intended Change table row: CONFIRM THESE ARE WANTED -> unchanged
criteria.reason: Present and unmodified in all four layers. The pre-existing gloss difference between the workflow script ('invented machinery, no objective named' / 'no source names them') and the command prompt ('no objective named') was deliberately left alone, per the criterion, and is not a failure.

criteria.statement: In /audit-prd specifically, a requirement found already implemented still renders as the imperative ALREADY BUILT, unchanged
criteria.cites: Intended Change table row: ALREADY BUILT (/audit-prd) -> unchanged
criteria.reason: 'ALREADY BUILT — name the file; decide whether the requirement survives' present verbatim in both /audit-prd layers.

criteria.statement: This change adds no new heading that groups multiple finding types under a single umbrella label — the heading count is unchanged except for the one split named in FS-6
criteria.cites: Intended Change: 'No grouping headings are added'
criteria.reason: The three named candidate umbrella strings (WHAT THE AUDIT CHANGED, WHAT NEEDS YOU, NOT CHECKED as a heading) have zero occurrences across all six files and their .claude mirrors. A full read of every heading block confirms each heading still labels exactly one finding type, and the only count change is FS-6's split of one heading into two.

criteria.statement: For the unchecked-claims finding, the readout reuses the spelling the clean path already emits — CAVEAT — and points at the document's own ## Could Not Verify section rather than reprinting it
criteria.cites: Intended Change: 'reuses the spelling the clean path already emits — CAVEAT — and points at the document rather than reprinting it'
criteria.reason: The findings-path heading reads 'CAVEAT — what this run did NOT check: <n> claims left unchecked (see the TRD's/PRD's ## Could Not Verify), plus any verifier that failed to report' — a pointer naming the section, with none of its contents inlined. The pre-existing clean-path CAVEAT for failed verifiers is untouched, so each workflow script carries two occurrences and both are pointer-shaped.

criteria.statement: Across every finding type, a heading describing something the audit already did reads in past tense, and a heading describing something only the owner can decide stays imperative
criteria.cites: Intended Change: 'a heading applied by the audit is past tense; a heading needing the owner stays imperative'
criteria.reason: Complete heading blocks read in all six files. Every audit-performed heading is past tense (DELETED, LOWERED, ADDED BACK, REDESIGNED, FIXED THE CITATION, CORRECTED A STALE CLAIM, REJECTED THESE FINDINGS); every owner-decision heading stays imperative (PICK ONE, CONFIRM THESE ARE WANTED, CANNOT BE BUILT, ALREADY BUILT). /audit-build's four named exceptions (TRACEABILITY GAPS, MISSING IMPLEMENTATION, MISMATCH, UNTESTED-IN-PRACTICE) correctly stay non-past-tense because that command writes no code or tests. No heading remains that both describes an audit-performed action and reads as an imperative — the FS-4 rename closed the last one.
